A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BioArc work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original DNA and protein evaluations, architecture-prediction results, ablations and a promoter interpretability case study.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds genomic benchmark results, a controlled protein comparison, pretraining-loss measurements and gradient-stability analyses.

M1.justification: The five-block search space, pruning procedures, weight-sharing supernet, three pretraining objectives, independent path finetuning, normalized ranking and architecture predictors are retained. Expanded sampling explanations and relocation of prediction methods to Appendix A.7.7 do not establish a change to BioArc's core procedure.

E1.justification: The original human GUE and six PEER tasks remain. v3 adds 18 Nucleotide Transformer benchmark tasks and nine Genomic Benchmarks datasets (Tables 7–8), extending coverage to histone marks, enhancers, open chromatin, coding/intergenic classification and species discrimination, including Drosophila and mouse data.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 7–8 introduce Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS and GENERator as comparators, with baseline scores explicitly reproduced from the GENERator paper. Table 2 adds a reimplemented ESM-2 8M under matched pretraining alongside retained released checkpoints. These comparisons are absent from v1; the architecture-prediction comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a protein comparison matching 8M parameters, full-UniRef50 pretraining and 50K steps, plus MCC evaluation on the added NT benchmark. Ranking evaluation now separates supernet-level from individual-path finetuning. New gradient tests use fixed mini-batches in a controlled 125-path supernet and the original supernet. Existing default training hyperparameters and predictor splits largely remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.7.6 newly tests shared-block gradient stability across paths in controlled and original supernets. A.7.5 replaces the single ranking analysis with two distinct comparisons. The promoter case study changes its example and adds gradient-weighted filter selection. Scaling, layer probes, hybrid-versus-pure comparisons and depth analyses already existed in v1 and are largely relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report across-architecture standard deviations, layer-probe standard errors and Spearman significance, without repeated-run counts, seeds or confidence intervals. Changed significance values and error bars are result changes. The added gradient-dispersion diagnostics do not introduce a distinct uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds NT/GB scores and matched protein results, including Fold scores of 20.75 for BioArc 8M versus 18.25 for reimplemented ESM-2; these are new settings, not gains over v1's BioArc rows. The single 0.8170 ranking correlation is replaced by 0.3222 and 0.7287 under differentiated protocols. Training-strategy results also change: Figure 9's protein mask-ft solubility win rate changes from 27.2% to 66.0%. Core DNA pretrained-model scores and predictor results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The CNN motif-location definition changes from maximizing the convolution response in v1 Equation 15 to maximizing its absolute magnitude in v3 Equation 14. Search-space definitions, losses, ranking and predictor mathematics otherwise remain equivalent after renumbering. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Efficient high-performing architectures, design guidelines and architecture prediction remain the central contributions. v3 explicitly elevates hierarchical biological-grammar capture into the abstract, introduction and conclusion, whereas v1 discusses it in the appendix. It also makes heterogeneous-search novelty more explicit without replacing the central research thesis.

C2.justification: v1 attributes protein structural-task weaknesses to pretraining scale and missing spatial positional bias, describing a performance ceiling. v3 rejects an architectural ceiling under matched budgets and attributes the remaining gap mainly to pretraining scale. It also replaces the interpretation of comparable masked and contrastive training with contrastive instability and task-dependent advantages, and qualifies direct supernet ranking through weight-interference evidence.

D1.justification: v3 supplies block configurations and fixed-mini-batch details for gradient tests and specifies the controlled protein pretraining budget. It removes v1's reproducibility statement and partial anonymized implementation link without replacement. Most existing hyperparameters, timings and prompts remain. Scaled-model documentation becomes inconsistent: Table 6 labels the model 88M, while Appendix A.6.3 retains 74.7M.

R1.justification: v3 adds BossNAS and DeepVirFinder discussion, sharpening the comparison with homogeneous or two-block NAS, and adds Caduceus, GENERator and Genomic Benchmarks references. RoFormer and some promoter references are removed. These refine the literature coverage and novelty positioning while retaining the broader biological-foundation-model and NAS framing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Dataset descriptions move into experimental settings, training and tokenization sections merge, and architecture prediction moves largely into Appendix A.7.7. Interpretability and analysis summaries become main-text sections, with substantial appendix reorganization.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column ICLR to two-column ICML formatting. Figure 1 replaces the agent panel with tokenization; training-strategy charts are redrawn; the promoter visualization is replaced and moved into the main text. The protein table gains a controlled-comparison block, new benchmark and gradient tables appear, and one ranking plot becomes two. Retained displays are extensively resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The matched-budget protein comparison and separate ranking controls strengthen evidence for architectural advantages, while added benchmarks broaden validation. However, v3 claims wins on all histone-mark tasks despite losses in Table 7, introduces conflicting 74.7M/88M model descriptions, and removes the implementation link. The stronger empirical support yields a limited net improvement, tempered by reporting and reproducibility weaknesses.
